name: a_overnight_policy
prompt:
Search the web now. You are a financial fact extractor for a US-equity pre-market brief.
Brief date: Monday October 5, 2026. Topic: Overnight & weekend policy.

Window: Friday October 2, 2026 4:00 PM ET (after the close) through Monday October 5, 2026 12:20 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. This spans 2 non-trading day(s): news published on those days (e.g. Saturday and Sunday) is in scope and often the most important. Anything published after 12:20 ET on Monday October 5, 2026 is out of scope.

FIND
Statements and actions since the session close by the President, Treasury Secretary, Commerce, USTR, Energy Secretary, Fed officials, and foreign leaders (China, Iran, Russia, EU): Sunday TV interviews, weekend summits, executive orders, scheduled White House meetings or announcements for the coming days, AI regulation remarks. Verbatim quotes with names and dates.

Run multiple searches with different phrasings and dates. Prefer primary sources and wire services
(Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, CNBC, WSJ, MarketWatch, Barron's, Investopedia, company press releases, SEC
EDGAR, BLS/BEA/Census/Fed releases, FDA). For every item give the latest status as of the cutoff.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or topic:

## TICKER or Topic `[Category]`
- fact (source)

Category: pick from AI Compute · Memory & Interconnect · Optical & Photonics · Chip Equipment · Fab & Foundry · Wireless & Mobile · Analog & Mixed-Signal · Power & Wide-Bandgap · Test & Advanced Packaging · Specialty Materials & IP Licensing · Quantum Computing · EdgeAI · Semiconductors · AI Infrastructure · Software & SaaS · Internet & Platforms · Communications & Networking, or Macro / Commodities / Geopolitics / Crypto / Calendar /
Pharma / Energy / Retail, or a concise sector name. Bold tickers.

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.
  "Analysts said" / "reports suggest" without a name is not allowed.
- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.
- Mark unconfirmed items (people familiar, leaks, social media, M&A speculation) with [rumor]. A
  Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ report citing sources is still reportable: state it and mark [report].
- If one event moved several stocks, name every stock and its move in the same bullet.
- Only facts published in the window. Older background only if it is the direct cause of a move in
  the window, labelled with its date.
- Do not interpret price action. Do not write "strong", "beat expectations", "investors cheered",
  "remains", "continues to", "well-positioned", "tailwinds". Write the number.
- Do not write bullets about what you could not find. Omit the topic instead.
- Do not drop facts to save space.
content:
## AI Regulation / **NVDA**, **META**, **GOOGL**, **MSFT**, **OPENAI** [AI Compute · Internet & Platforms · Software & SaaS]

- President Donald Trump announced on October 4 that he appointed National Intelligence Director Jay Clayton, Federal Trade Commission Chairman Andrew Ferguson, Office of Personnel Management Director Scott Kupor, and Pentagon research and technology official Emil Michael to lead a federal “Super Intelligence Force” coordinating government engagement with AI companies, consumers, public-interest groups, critical-infrastructure providers, and religious organizations; the force will report to Trump and White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles. [report] (Reuters, Oct. 4; updated Oct. 5 00:03 ET)
- Trump said the task force would “ensure that America continues to lead the World in Super Intelligence,” which he described as potentially larger than the Industrial Revolution and the internet. (AP, Oct. 4; updated Oct. 5 05:25 ET)
- Trump’s October 4 announcement followed a September 29 White House meeting with AI executives from Nvidia, SpaceX, OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, and Alphabet’s Google, at which participating companies signed a voluntary accord calling for robust internal controls and independent external audits. (Reuters, Oct. 4; updated Oct. 5 00:03 ET)
- Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Axios that AI companies should police themselves and criticized warnings about existential AI risks; when asked about calls from AI executives for regulation, Bessent said, “Well, then they should slow down.” (Axios, Oct. 3; updated Oct. 4 20:03 ET)
- Bessent said the United States and China planned a bilateral AI-notification system intended to share warnings about serious incidents and reduce uncertainty; he said the Treasury Department and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng had agreed to create a “U.S.-China AI dialogue.” (Axios, Oct. 3; updated Oct. 4 20:03 ET)

## **XLE**, **VLO**, **MPC**, **PSX** / Europe Diesel Reserves [Energy]

- President Donald Trump said on October 2 that European countries had agreed to release diesel reserves after EU governments discussed a French proposal for Europe to release 50 million barrels of diesel and for International Energy Agency members to release 50 million barrels of crude oil. [report] (Reuters, Oct. 2 11:13 ET)
- Reuters reported that the United States had urged France and Germany to release emergency diesel inventories and had sought releases totaling 100 million barrels within 20 days; the discussions followed US consideration of a diesel-export ban amid fuel-price disruptions linked to the Iran war. [report] (Reuters, Oct. 2 11:13 ET)
- The Group of Seven agreed to release 100 million barrels of crude oil and fuel from emergency reserves, according to a trade publication report dated October 3; the report said the agreement reduced the immediate risk of a European and Mexican supply disruption. [report] (Washington Trade & Tariff, Oct. 3; updated Oct. 5 07:47 ET)

## Russia Sanctions / **XLE**, **OXY**, **LNG** [Macro / Geopolitics / Energy]

- US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said the administration had not ruled out imposing secondary sanctions on Russia’s trade partners by October 18 under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act; when asked whether President Trump would impose tariffs or sanctions by that date, Wright said Trump “leaves every decision till the end” and would evaluate the trade-offs. (CBS News interview, reported Oct. 5 03:11 ET)
- Wright said the administration was examining “every leverage” available to end the Ukraine conflict and lower prices for Americans. (CBS News interview, reported Oct. 5 03:11 ET)

## China Trade Policy / **BABA**, **PDD**, **JD**, **XPEV** [Macro / Geopolitics]

- China’s Commerce Ministry said on October 4 that the Group of 20 trade ministers’ meeting had exposed divisions over US-backed trade proposals; the ministry said the meeting’s joint statement opposed weaponization of food through coercive trade practices but did not reach consensus on forced labor in supply chains or excess industrial capacity. (China Commerce Ministry, reported Oct. 5 04:04 ET)
- China’s Commerce Ministry said the G20 meeting moved away from a US proposal to revise most-favored-nation trade rules. (China Commerce Ministry, reported Oct. 5 04:04 ET)

## Iran Conflict / Diesel Supply [Macro / Commodities / Geopolitics]

- Reuters reported on October 2 that Washington was sending additional warships and troops to the region, while Iranian officials were preparing a “broad and forceful response”; Reuters said diplomatic efforts were continuing. [report] (Reuters, Oct. 2 07:29 ET)
- A report published October 4 said President Trump was considering resuming major combat operations in Iran after negotiations stalled; the report attributed the information to Axios and said senior cabinet members had met at Camp David to discuss next steps. [report] (Asharq Al-Awsat, Oct. 4; updated Oct. 5 05:51 ET)
